sermon.title: Adding Godliness
sermon.series: Bible Morality Banned by Wimps and Born by Warriors
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: The speaker defines godliness as the condition of respecting and obeying God, and says the Bible’s definition of godliness is Jesus Christ (1 Timothy 3:16). He teaches that godliness is profitable for this life and the next (1 Timothy 4:8), contrasts it with humanism and Christian humanism (1 Timothy 6; 2 Timothy 3; Titus 1:16), argues Great Society policies did not end poverty, and urges holy conduct and godliness that hasten the day of the Lord (2 Peter 3).
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added by hand, and obvious caption errors were corrected; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Caption corrections include verse colon formatting, “You can’t be satisfied” for “it can be satisfied,” “Christian humanists” for “Christians humanists,” and “why are Christians divorcing” for “why of Christians divorcing.” He cites statistics (STD/AIDS 30k, alcohol 85k, drugs 17k, tobacco 450k, child sexual abuse 460k; poverty/jobless/hunger rates flat since Johnson; $17 trillion) without sources—flagged unverified. Names Lyndon B. Johnson. Sensitive claims on homosexuality, child abuse, lying by president/Congress/teachers kept as spoken. Speaker not named in recording; series continuity attributes Pastor David G. Kincer—confirm.

chunks.section_question: What is godliness, according to the dictionary and the Bible?
chunks.short_answer: He says godly means respecting and obeying God, and -ness means the condition of—so godliness is possessing that condition. The dictionary definition is that; the Bible definition of godliness is Jesus Christ, citing 1 Timothy 3:16.

The Bible definition of godliness is Jesus Christ. First Timothy 3:16.

He says this is clear scripture that Jesus was God in the flesh and that Jesus possessed the condition of respecting and obeying God.
chunks.text: Great is the mystery, the hidden thing of godliness. Mystery is something hidden. It’s not hidden anymore. Number one, God was manifest—visible—he appeared in the flesh. Here’s another scripture that says Jesus is God. For those who want to debate that Jesus was only the Son of God, here’s another clear scripture that Jesus was God in the flesh. Justified in the Spirit: when Jesus was baptized, a dove came down, the Holy Spirit in the form of a dove. He was seen by angels. Angels appeared both at his birth and before his birth, after he was tempted in the wilderness, and the angel rolled the stone away. Among—he preached among the Gentiles. God preached among the Gentiles in the body of Jesus Christ. He was believed on in the world, both with Gentiles and Jews, even though he said, I’ve not called but to the Jews and not the Gentiles. He was received up after he died on the cross. So Jesus possessed the condition of respecting and obeying God.

Godliness is profitable for obtaining two promises.
chunks.text: All right, now godliness is part of the growing, the changing process which results in good works for Christians. First Timothy 2:10. After saying, telling women not to let it be the adorning of the outward, he says but that which becomes a woman—that’s which is proper for a woman, suitable for a woman professing godliness with good works. Now this word becomes, as I said, means proper or suitable. If you’re going to profess godliness, you should be acting right, behaving right. But it also means to grow into, like the caterpillar. Caterpillar becomes a butterfly. The caterpillar goes into the cocoon and grows and develops and changes into a totally new, different kind of creature—from an ugly creature to a beautiful butterfly. chunks.section_question: What two promises does he say godliness is profitable for?
chunks.short_answer: He reads 1 Timothy 4:7–8 to exercise yourself toward godliness, which has promise of the life that now is and of that which is to come. He says godly Christians avoid preventable deaths and costs from AIDS, STDs, alcohol, drugs, and tobacco, and that godliness is important for eternal life, not only faith and grace.
chunks.text: First Timothy 4:7, exercise, train, discipline yourself. You know we do this bodily exercising and all this, but we’ve got to train and exercise ourselves toward godliness, because godliness is profitable for all things, having two promises: the promise of life that now is, and that which is to come. Godly Christians in this life avoid preventable deaths, injuries, and medical costs of AIDS and sexually transmitted diseases, which take thirty thousand lives a year in America. Alcohol takes 85,000; drugs 17,000; tobacco 450,000; and 460,000 children are sexually abused every year. Godly Christians don’t do these things, and it gives you eternal life. Everybody’s always talking about faith and grace to get eternal life. This plainly says godliness is important for eternal life now.

chunks.short_answer: He reads 1 Timothy 6:3–5 that anyone who will not consent to the wholesome words of Jesus or doctrine agreeing with godliness is proud, knows nothing, and is obsessed with disputes. He says withdraw from those who treat godliness as a means of wealth, and that godliness with contentment is great gain.
chunks.text: God’s view, God’s description of humanism and its followers. First Timothy 6:3, if anyone teaches otherwise and does not consent to wholesome words, even to the words of our Lord Jesus Christ—we have no right to teach what Jesus didn’t teach—or to the doctrine which agrees with godliness, that condition of respecting God and obeying him. If someone does that, he is proud. You’re just a proud, cocky, arrogant person, and gee, God says you don’t know anything. You’re obsessed with disputes and arguments over words. People today just arguing and debate about nonsense. Who suppose godliness is a means of gain or a means of wealth—from such withdraw yourself. Get away from these people. They will infect you with their unwholesome words and their own words instead of Christ. And then he goes on to say, now godliness with contentment is great gain. See, having the condition of respecting God and obeying God with being satisfied where you’re at.

chunks.section_question: Did Lyndon Johnson’s Great Society end poverty, according to the sermon?
chunks.short_answer: He says in 1964 Johnson called for ending poverty, joblessness, and hunger; he calls him a humanist and liberal. He cites poverty, jobless, and hunger rates still about 15% / 40% / 15% by 2014 after $17 trillion of debt, and says it did not work because Jesus said the poor you have always (Matthew 26:11; Deuteronomy 15:11).

Okay, they’re going to stamp out—he’s a humanist. He was a liberal. But when you look at the facts, the proper poverty rate back in 1965 was 15%; 2014, 15%. Jobless rate—the adults that can work that wasn’t working—in 1970, 40%; to 2014, 40%. The hunger rate 1965 15%, 2014 15%. They did not eradicate hunger, poverty, or the jobless, but they did spend 17 trillion dollars going in debt, and a lot of that money was trying to eradicate poverty and hunger and joblessness. It didn’t work. Why? Because Jesus said in Matthew 26:11, you will have the poor with you always. You’re not going to change the word of God. The poor is going to be around, and that proves the Bible’s true, by the way, people looking for proof. Deuteronomy 15:11, the poor will never cease out of the land. Matthew 24, there will be wars, famines, earthquakes, troubles. And we have wars, famines, and earthquakes, and these people can’t do a thing about it. Why? Because God said it’s going to be.

He reads 2 Timothy 3 that in the last days men will have a form of godliness but deny its power, ever learning and never able to come to the truth—from such turn away. He says stay away so you are not tainted, yet reach them as a harvest field.

Remember the Bible says our faith is not to be in the intellect of men but in the power of God, and God has power to bring this about. Ever learning and never able to come to the recognition of the truth. These also reject the truth—men of corrupt minds. From such turn away. chunks.section_question: Why is godliness serious in light of the day of the Lord?
chunks.short_answer: He reads 2 Peter 3:10–12 that the heavens will pass away and the earth be burned up, so what manner of people ought you to be in holy conduct and godliness, looking for and hastening the coming of the day of the Lord. He says Jesus is coming for a mature, blameless church the gates of hell cannot prevail against—not today or tomorrow as we are.
chunks.text: The seriousness of godliness for all people. Second Peter 3:10, the Lord’s day will come as a thief in the night. The heavens will pass away with a great noise. Elements will melt with fervent heat. The earth and the works in it will be burned up. Therefore, since all these things will be dissolved, what manner of people ought you to be in holy conduct and godliness, looking for and hastening—speeding up—the coming of the day of the Lord. That’s a serious thing. He’s going to renovate this earth by fire, and we’re going to be accountable to our conduct and did we measure up to godliness and good works and godliness and conduct. Will speed up the coming of the Lord. So there has to be a visitation, coming of God that’s going to turn the church to godliness. He’s not coming today. He’s not coming tomorrow. He’s coming for a church that is mature, the gates of hell cannot prevail against, that is blameless and righteous and holy, and he has the power to accomplish that. And he will accomplish it.

chunks.section_question: What should gathering as a church be for?

Church should stir people to godliness and good works, not entertainment or flattery. He says the early church would rather die or stay in prison than deny Christ, and that Jesus—not Christian or secular humanists—will win by a visitation of godliness.
chunks.text: And so we see the seriousness of the situation. Christian humanists must reconsider their beliefs. In Hebrews 10:24, consider one another to provoke one another and to love and do good works, not forsaking the assembling of yourselves together. When we come to church it should be for the purpose of encouraging, stirring up people to godliness and doing good works. Shouldn’t be for entertainment and patting each other on the back and flattering each other, but exhort one another, encourage one another. You see, the early church died—and whereas in prison rather—than deny Christ. See, they obtained this thing. They wouldn’t deny truth. They wouldn’t deny godliness. Christian nor secular humanists will win. They won’t get the last word. Jesus will win by a visitation of godliness before returning for his blameless, prevailing-over-the-gates-of-hell and mature bride. The bride has made herself ready. He is making his church ready. There is a visitation coming.

He says with power we do not commit homosexuality, adultery, or child sexual abuse, and we do not lie like the president, Congress, governors, school teachers, and textbooks. Godliness does not embrace lying; there is power in godliness because there is power in the God we serve.

There’s power in godliness, because there’s power in the God that we serve. Thank you.

faqs.answer: He says we do bodily exercising, but we must train and exercise ourselves toward godliness because it is profitable for all things with promise for this life and the life to come.

scriptures.text_nkjv: But reject profane and old wives’ fables, and exercise yourself toward godliness. For bodily exercise profits a little, but godliness is profitable for all things, having promise of the life that now is and of that which is to come.

faqs.question: What does he say about godliness with contentment?
faqs.answer: He says godliness with contentment is great gain—having the condition of respecting and obeying God while being satisfied where you are at—and to withdraw from those who treat godliness as a means of wealth.

scriptures.text_nkjv: Now godliness with contentment is great gain.

faqs.question: What does Matthew 26:11 mean for anti-poverty programs in this sermon?
faqs.answer: He says Jesus said you will have the poor with you always, so you are not going to change the word of God; the poor will be around, which he says proves the Bible true (also Deuteronomy 15:11).

scriptures.text_nkjv: For you have the poor with you always, but Me you do not have always.
For the poor will never cease from the land; therefore I command you, saying, ‘You shall open your hand wide to your brother, to your poor and your needy, in your land.’

faqs.question: What does “add to” mean for godliness after salvation?
faqs.answer: He says add to means you did not have it before—you did not get it when you got saved, confessed, repented, were water baptized, or baptized in the Holy Ghost; you have to add it to your life.

faqs.question: What is a “form of godliness” that denies its power?
faqs.answer: He says in the last days men will have an appearance of godliness but deny its power; faith is not to be in the intellect of men but in the power of God—from such turn away.

scriptures.text_nkjv: But know this, that in the last days perilous times will come: For men will be lovers of themselves, lovers of money, boasters, proud, blasphemers, disobedient to parents, unthankful, unholy, unloving, unforgiving, slanderers, without self-control, brutal, despisers of good, traitors, headstrong, haughty, lovers of pleasure rather than lovers of God, having a form of godliness but denying its power. And from such people turn away!

faqs.question: What kind of church does he say Jesus is coming for?
faqs.answer: He says Jesus is not coming today or tomorrow; he is coming for a mature church the gates of hell cannot prevail against, that is blameless, righteous, and holy, and he has the power to accomplish that.

scriptures.text_nkjv: But the day of the Lord will come as a thief in the night, in which the heavens will pass away with a great noise, and the elements will melt with fervent heat; both the earth and the works that are in it will be burned up. Therefore, since all these things will be dissolved, what manner of persons ought you to be in holy conduct and godliness, looking for and hastening the coming of the day of God, because of which the heavens will be dissolved, being on fire, and the elements will melt with fervent heat?

faqs.question: What does he say the early church would rather do than deny Christ?
faqs.answer: He says they would rather die, and stay in prison rather than deny Christ; they would not deny truth or godliness.

faqs.question: What “visitation of godliness” does he expect before Jesus returns?
faqs.answer: He says Jesus will win by a visitation of godliness before returning for his blameless, mature bride; the bride has made herself ready, and he is making his church ready.

faqs.question: Does godliness allow lying?
faqs.answer: He says godliness does not embrace lying, and contrasts that with lying by the president, Congress, governors, school teachers, and textbooks; there is power in godliness because there is power in God.
